summary:
The name of this bill is the Citizen Investment Trust (Third Amendment) Bill, 2083 (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 1). This bill has been introduced to encourage the general public to save capital for the economic development of the country, increase investment opportunities, run retirement fund and social security programs, bring dynamism to the capital market, clarify certain terms defined by the Act, increase the authorized capital, paid-up capital and share investment of the Trust, adjust the capital of the Trust, and further clarify the functions, duties and powers of the Board of Directors and the Executive Director (Objectives and Reasons). This Act shall come into force immediately (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

Any amount invested in fixed deposits in any commercial bank or infrastructure development bank, along with its interest or any other fees, must be paid by the concerned bank to the Trust in accordance with the agreement made between the Trust and that bank (Section 15, Subsection 2, Page 4). Within three months after the end of the fiscal year, the Trust must prepare its balance sheet and profit and loss account, have them signed by the Executive Director, the employee working as the head of accounting, and at least two directors, and submit them to the Government of Nepal (Section 10, Page 3).

In the Board of Directors of the Citizen Investment Trust, provisions are made for the Chief Executive Officer of Rastriya Jeevan Beema Company Limited and one director elected or nominated from among financial institutions and insurance companies (Section 5, Subsection 1, Page 1). The tenure of the nominated and elected director shall be three years and they may be nominated and elected once more (Section 5, Subsection 2, Page 1). An officer employee of the Trust shall act as the secretary of the Board (Section 5, Subsection 3, Page 1). The Board of Directors shall have the duties to make necessary policy arrangements for the activities of the Trust, prepare and implement internal control systems and risk management standards, prepare an appropriate organizational structure and submit it to the Government of Nepal, Ministry of Finance for approval, submit the annual audit report along with the annual report to the General Assembly, and perform other tasks specified by the Government of Nepal (Section 7, Subsection 1, Page 2). The Board may delegate some of its powers to any director, subcommittee, Executive Director, or officer-level employee of the Trust (Section 7, Subsection 2, Page 2). The tenure of the Executive Director of the Trust shall be four years and they may be re-appointed once, but the Government of Nepal may remove the Executive Director at any time (Section 11, Subsection 1a, 1b, Page 3). The Executive Director shall exercise powers received from the Board under prevailing law, supervise and control the activities and transactions of the Trust, prepare the annual budget and action plan and submit them to the Board for approval, manage manpower under employee regulations, implement decisions of the General Assembly and Board, operate the Trust in accordance with directives of regulatory bodies, manage internal control and risk management, act in the best interest of the Trust, shareholders, contributors and participants, and perform other tasks specified by the Board (Section 12, Subsection 1, Page 3). The Executive Director may delegate powers such as fund management, fund mobilization, litigation defense, and running daily administration to any officer employee of the Trust (Section 12, Subsection 2, Page 3). The authorized capital of the Trust shall be Rs. 10 billion divided into 100 million shares at the rate of Rs. 100 per share, and the paid-up capital shall be Rs. 6.80 billion (Section 3, Subsection 1, 2, Page 1). The Board of Directors may alter the share capital and its allotment and structure with prior approval of the Government of Nepal, Council of Ministers, and may increase paid-up capital within the limit of issued capital with prior approval of the Government of Nepal, Ministry of Finance (Section 4, Subsection 1, 2, Page 1). The Trust may invest funds from the Investment Account Scheme, Citizen Unit Scheme, and its own resources in fixed deposits of Infrastructure Development Banks recognized by the Government of Nepal or Nepal Rastra Bank, in securities of commercial banks, financial institutions, insurance companies, mutual funds, private equity funds or venture capital funds registered with the Securities Board of Nepal, and in debentures or bonds (Section 8, Subsection 1, 3, Page 2, 3). The Trust may provide loans to national priority projects related to energy, transport, tourism, information technology, agriculture, health and education sectors, invest in housing projects and provide loans to participants to purchase houses and land plots, and operate portfolio management services to support the development of the capital market (Section 8, Subsection 2, 3, Page 2, 3).
